_comment: Written by deploy/eggs/egg.py. Do not edit: edit deploy/eggs/ and run it again.
name: Overtone db
author: dev@midesprojects.com
description: PostgreSQL for Overtone, from the official image, with its data in /home/container/pgdata so the panel's backups and disk limit cover it. One server for both environments: a database per environment.

config.startup: {"done": "database system is ready to accept connections"}

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Install script of the overtone-db egg.
#
# Nothing to download: the official postgres image initialises PGDATA on its
# first start, as the panel's user, with POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_PASSWORD and
# POSTGRES_DB. This only checks that a reinstall will not hide an existing
# cluster behind a new password: the image reads those variables when PGDATA
# is empty and never again.
set -euo pipefail

mkdir -p /mnt/server
if [ -f /mnt/server/pgdata/PG_VERSION ]; then
    echo "[overtone-db] /home/container/pgdata already holds a PostgreSQL $(cat /mnt/server/pgdata/PG_VERSION) cluster; kept as it is."
    echo "[overtone-db] POSTGRES_PASSWORD and POSTGRES_DB are not applied to it again."
else
    echo "[overtone-db] empty; the first start creates the cluster in /home/container/pgdata."
fi

variables.name: Port
variables.description: The server's allocation port. PostgreSQL listens where PGPORT says, and Wings maps the allocation to the same port inside the container.

variables.name: Superuser
variables.description: Created on the first start, with the password below. The apps never use it: each environment gets its own role (docs/deploy.md).

variables.name: Superuser password
variables.description: At least 24 characters. Read on the first start only; change it later with ALTER ROLE.

variables.name: First database
variables.description: Created on the first start: production's.

variables.name: Data directory
variables.description: Under /home/container, or the data is outside the server's disk and its backups.
